mechanism_narrative: The observed consistent week-over-week increase in RETAIL_REC mobility over the last four weeks indicates a sustained recovery trend that will continue, driving further increases in retail activity over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: The mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is equal to or lower than the mean RETAIL_REC over the last 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: A significant week-on-week increase in WORKPLACES mobility, as seen at t-0w, suggests a return to office work that will boost lunchtime and after-work retail and recreation activity over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES increases by more than 3 points week-on-week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not show an increase in its weekly mean over the next two weeks following a trigger event.

mechanism_narrative: The concurrent increase in both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES mobility signifies a broader return to urban commuting, which directly translates to increased foot traffic and spending in retail and recreation venues over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than the last 28 days, despite both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES showing sustained increases.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in RESIDENTIAL mobility coupled with an increase in GROCERY_PHARM mobility, especially when both are moving away from baseline, indicates people are spending less time at home and more time out for essential errands, which will spill over into non-essential retail over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase over the next four weeks when RESIDENTIAL decreases and GROCERY_PHARM increases.

mechanism_narrative: A significant week-on-week drop in PARKS mobility, as observed at t-0w, suggests a temporary weather-related dip that will likely rebound quickly, boosting outdoor-adjacent retail and recreation activity in the immediate next week.
candidate_trigger: PARKS mobility drops by more than 4 points week-on-week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC decreases in the next week, despite a rebound in PARKS mobility.

mechanism_narrative: The broad-based recovery observed across RETAIL_REC, GROCERY_PHARM, and TRANSIT, all showing less negative values, indicates a general increase in public activity and confidence that will sustain the upward trend in retail and recreation over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: The average RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is not higher than the average of the last 28 days, despite all three proxies showing continued recovery.

mechanism_narrative: The recent decrease in RESIDENTIAL mobility at t-1w, followed by a slight increase at t-0w, suggests a fluctuating but overall trend of people spending less time at home, which will gradually free up time for retail and recreation over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL mobility falls below 14.0 percent change from baseline
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase over the next two weeks when RESIDENTIAL mobility consistently stays below 14.0.

mechanism_narrative: A strong increase in WORKPLACES mobility combined with RESIDENTIAL mobility remaining below 15.0 indicates a clear shift from home-based activities to work-related commuting, which will immediately boost local retail and recreation near workplaces in the upcoming week.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES increases by more than 3 points week-on-week, while RESIDENTIAL remains below 15.0 percent change from baseline
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC decreases in the next week, despite a significant rise in WORKPLACES and RESIDENTIAL remaining below 15.0.
